subject: Recap + ask: hosted API burn, budget range & peak TPS for Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + ask: hosted API burn, budget range & peak TPS for Aurelia Health

Carlos — great demo earlier, thanks for carving out the time. Quick recap and two asks so we can put a formal pricing recommendation together for your procurement/prod teams.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: conversational summarization + structured triage for patient intake (web + mobile).
- Expected ramp: pilot in May (month 1: small cohort), followed by phased rollout across clinics over 6–12 months.
- Typical per-call tokens: ~45–85 tokens (summary + metadata), average ~64 tokens per interaction based on your sample.

Pricing qualification asks (please confirm by reply):
1) Expected monthly token volume range once live (select one):
   - A: 5–15M
   - B: 15–40M
   - C: 40–80M
2) Expected short-window peak TPS (99th percentile) during batch/clinic spike windows. If you don’t have an exact number, give us the highest concurrent requests you expect in any 60s window.
3) Target $/1M tokens you are budgeting for (ballpark is fine).

Preliminary Redwood guidance (for context)
- If you land in range B, hosted committed pricing typically lands in the $36–46 per 1M tokens band (volume + 30-day commit).
- For C-level volumes (40M+), we can propose a blended $/1M with burst headroom and reserve slabs; example: $34–40/1M for 60M+ commits plus a short-window burst surcharge for peak TPS.
- Peak TPS considerations: for conversational traffic with 64 tokens/interaction, 350 TPS sustained for short bursts corresponds to ~1.7M tokens in 10 minutes — we’d want autoscale + KV prefix caching to control cost.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short pricing primer and the traffic sample you shared back to us so we’re aligned.

Next steps
- Carlos: confirm the three asks above.
- Rachel/Marissa: will produce a 1-page pricing scenario (committed bands + burst options) and a suggested SLO/retention profile for procurement.

Thanks — I’ll aim to get a scenario doc to you within 24–48 hours after we have the numbers.

—
Rachel Kim
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference — hosted inference for production LLMs

Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_Pricing_1M_slide.pdf (pdf), Aurelia_TRAFFIC_SAMPLE.csv (csv)

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Apr 2028 09:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: hosted API burn, budget range & peak TPS for Aurelia Health

Rachel — quick answers inline. Appreciate the clear recap.

1) Expected monthly token volume: C (40–80M) is the right bucket for planning. We’re targeting 40–60M in the first 6 months post-pilot; long-term upside if rollout is faster.

2) Peak TPS: two sources of spikes — (a) morning clinic surge windows (08:00–09:00 local) and (b) nightly batch processing (report generation). For the clinic surge we anticipate short bursts up to ~300–400 concurrent requests (not sustained more than 10–15 minutes). For nightly batch runs, we may have scheduled bursts that look like 700 TPS for 5–10 minutes (these are controlled jobs we can throttle).

3) Target $/1M tokens: procurement is aiming for ~ $40/1M as a budget target for hosted. If we can get steady-state credits/discounts with a committed band, that helps.

Procurement note: please include basic responses on data residency (US-only), retention windows (30/90/365 options), and SOC2/HIPAA posture in your follow-up. Also send the traffic sample that I uploaded earlier (attached).

Carlos
Carlos Mendez
VP Product, Aurelia Health
carlos.mendez@aureliahealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Attachments: Aurelia_TRAFFIC_SAMPLE.csv (from our side)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Apr 2028 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: hosted API burn, budget range & peak TPS for Aurelia Health

Carlos — perfect, thanks for the detail. Below is a tight preliminary cost/ops sketch so procurement has something concrete while Marissa and I draft the official scenario doc + SOW.

Assumptions (from your numbers)
- Planning monthly token window: 60M tokens (midpoint of 40–80M).
- Avg tokens per request: 64 (from your sample).
- Baseline QPS (steady state): 60M tokens / 30 days / 86400s * (1 / 64 tokens/request) ≈ 10–12 QPS baseline.
- Peak bursts: clinic windows up to 400 concurrent, nightly batch up to 700 TPS (5–10 minutes).

Suggested Hosted plan (short list):
1) Committed slab: 60M/month at $38/1M tokens = $2,280/month (committed billing). This assumes a 12-month rolling commit with standard hosted SLAs.
2) Burst headroom: short-window burst pricing for TPS > baseline — we typically offer a burst pool priced at +22–30% over committed $/1M for on-demand spikes (applied only to tokens consumed during bursts).
3) Autoscale + cache: enable prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts to cut variable token spend by ~8–18% depending on reuse. We’ll include recommendations in the scenario doc.

Operational notes for procurement
- Data residency: Redwood hosted supports regionally isolated clusters (US-only option available).
- Retention: configurable 30/90/365 day retention profiles; standard logs retained 90 days unless otherwise requested.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II in place; we have HIPAA BAAs for covered workflows — I’ll include the compliance packet in the follow-up.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short pricing slide that shows the committed slab example and burst math. Also re-attaching the traffic sample you sent so we’re both looking at the same row counts.

Next steps (we’ll take these once you confirm)
- Marissa & I: produce a 1-page Mutual Action Plan + pricing scenarios (committed 60M, stretch 80M, and pilot 5M) + brief SOW appendix for procurement.
- Carlos: confirm whether you want burst headroom as a purchased pool (recommended) or to rely on on-demand billing.
- Procurement: please share any procurement templates/standard clauses early if you want draft redlines.

I’ll follow up with the scenario doc and a short runbook for handling the 700 TPS nightly bursts (throttling + backoff guidance).

—
Rachel Kim
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_Pricing_1M_slide.pdf, Aurelia_TRAFFIC_SAMPLE.csv

Subject: Re: Recap + ask: hosted API burn, budget range & peak TPS for Aurelia Health

Rachel — thanks for the draft. Internal quick note / next actions I’ll take: 

- I will draft the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and attach a short SOW appendix covering the burst-pool option (decision point for them).
- I’ll also prepare a one-page DocuSign-ready quote that reflects:
   * Pilot: 5M tokens (trial credits)
   * Committed band: 60M @ $38/1M (baseline proposal)
   * Burst pool: prepaid 10M tokens @ +25% uplift applied only to burst-consumed tokens
- Rachel: please include the 700 TPS runbook appendix (throttling controls + recommended autoscale buffer).
- Rachel/Marissa: propose a call next Wed to review MAP with Aurelia. I’ll include procurement and legal if Carlos confirms.

I’ll get a draft MAP + quote into the HubSpot deal and link the DocuSign powerform so Carlos/procurement can start onboarding.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
